curriculum.lesson_evidence: Throwing and catching are fundamental movement skills. For an overarm throw stand side-on to the target, look at the target, step forward with the foot opposite the throwing arm, bring the arm back, release and follow through across the body. To catch, keep your eyes on the ball, hold your hands ready in front, catch with your fingers and let your elbows give so the ball is cushioned. Use a soft ball and make sure nobody is in the throwing path.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Ella catches by trapping the ball against her chest and often drops it. Suggest two cues that would help her and say why.

FEEDBACK
Cues: 'eyes on the ball with hands ready' and 'let your elbows give as it lands in your hands'. Hands cushion better than the chest, and giving slows the ball. Hands shaped like a basket make a bigger target.

WATCH FOR
Thinking a harder throw is a better throw. An accurate, controlled throw with a follow through is easier to catch and safer for everyone.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Using a soft ball (or a rolled-up pair of socks) and a wall target, practise 10 throws and 10 catches at two different distances. Record how many hit the target or were caught, choose one cue to improve and retest. Make sure nobody is in the throwing path.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.
